newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine seeks $500 mln investments for industry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine seeks $500 mln investments for industry.

text.p: Ukraine hopes to attract $500 million in private foreign investment this year to upgrade industrial companies to make them more efficient, Industry Minister Valeriy Mazur said on Monday.

"The Ukrainian government is putting all possible effort into legally providing stable conditions for Ukrainian and foreign investors," Mazur told a news conference, where he distributed a list of some 60 enterprises seeking investment.

"The position of the ministry and government is to maximise privatisation of not only small enterprises but large, strategic enterprises," he said, adding that new tax reform laws would ease conditions and provide tax breaks for foreign investors.
Ukrainian politicians have recently made a push to boost foreign investment, totalling only $1.4 billion in the last five years, by promising to change investment conditions.
Foreign investors complain about demands for bribes, complex laws and high taxes, and some have had to meet President Leonid Kuchma to clear the way for their projects.
Ukraine attracted $459 million dollars in foreign investment in 1996.

Mazur did not specify which of the enterprises in the metallurgical, chemical, timber and light industry sectors would be sold outright, made available for strategic investment, or in which the government would keep a 26 percent stake.
The list named steel makers AT Azovstal and AT Zaporizhstal, fertiliser and oxygen manufacturers, AT Lvivfanprom match maker and several furniture builders, and textile and leather companies.
Parliament is reviewing the tax reform package, which will underpin the 1997 budget. Both documents are due to be passed this month or next.
Mazur cited one Ukrainian-Spanish joint-venture company which did not have to pay bribes and was happy with the legal climate and tax rules.
"If the legislative ground is not good enough, the government can make rules," he said. "A presidential decree can be issued. There are no problems."
